Hi Sam —

Great to sync today — appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps. I'll attach a short SDK setup guide (redwood-sdk-setup.pdf) and a sample request/response stub for both chat (tool-calling) and completion styles.

Recap / quick answers:
- Auth: Private deployment supports API keys + customer-managed KMS for key rotation. mTLS is supported for dedicated/private connectors; we'll share config snippets in the SDK doc.
- SDK setup: The official Redwood SDK has simple clients for generation, chat, and embeddings. We'll include code for routing requests to generation vs embeddings endpoints and how to wire in your retriever.
- Structured output & tool calling: Recommended pattern is to use the chat API with a tool-calling schema that enforces a JSON object in the assistant's reply. Use explicit schema validation in your app to avoid partial-tool emissions. Stop tokens still apply — for streaming we stream tokens but emit a final validated tool payload at the end (see streaming semantics below).
- Embeddings/reranker: Start with 512 token chunking for text fields that are <2k tokens; for long docs we recommend 256-512 chunk sizes and a hybrid rerank that uses embeddings for recall + a model-based rerank for precision.
- Tokenization / max_tokens: Token accounting depends on model family. For our recommended open models default max_tokens for completion endpoints is 2048; chat endpoints reserve ~200 tokens for system+meta by default — we'll include model-specific numbers. Streaming will still count tokens as they are emitted; truncation happens at the model max but we recommend truncation checks client-side for deterministic behavior.

Streaming semantics (short):
- We stream token deltas over a persistent SSE/WebSocket. 
- Partial content can be streamed, but we do NOT surface partial tool-call JSON as final until validation passes. The SDK exposes a "tool_call_start" / "tool_call_end" signal so clients can render partial output safely.

2) Dev Patel will send a sample chat+tool-call request/response example + SDK snippets (Dev).
3) Team to schedule a 30-min PoC kickoff next week to align on retriever and reranker approach (I'll send Doodle).

Hi Sam —

Following up with more technical detail and a minimal request/response example you can drop into your PoC. Summary of key points first, then the example.

Key clarifications:
- Chat vs completions: Use chat API for multi-turn dialogs and tool-calling. Completions are fine for single-shot generation. Chat API includes role metadata and is preferred when you need structured assistant actions.
- Max tokens & tokenization: Model X (open-llm-x) tokenizes similarly to common byte-pair approaches; we include a tokenization table in the SDK docs. For safety use model-specific max_tokens (2048 for X, 4096 for Y).
- Stop behavior: Stop tokens are applied to the generated token stream; in streaming mode they can trigger an immediate close of the token stream, but you'll still need to validate the final payload.
- Streaming & tool calling: The SDK exposes a streaming iterator; we send interleaved events for "partial_text", "tool_call_start", "tool_call_payload_fragment", and "tool_call_end". Client should buffer payload_fragments until tool_call_end and then run schema validation.

Minimal chat + tool-call example (pseudo-request):
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
Body: {
  "model": "open-llm-x-chat",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are a structured assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Lookup customer by id and return JSON"}],
  "tools": [{"name":"customer_lookup","schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"customer_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["customer_id"]}}],
  "stream": true
}

Stream events you should expect (simplified):
- partial_text: "Looking up customer..."
- tool_call_start: {"name":"customer_lookup"}
- tool_call_payload_fragment: "{\"customer_id\": \"12345\"}" (multiple fragments possible)
- tool_call_end: {}
- final_assistant_message: {"type":"tool_result","content":"{...validated JSON...}"}

Embedding + rerank notes:
- Compute embeddings for both query and chunks. Use cosine similarity for initial retrieval (top-K ~ 50), then apply a lightweight model-based rerank on the top 10-20 to improve precision.
- For short text fields prefer 768-dim embeddings; for long docs test 1024-dim profiles for recall.

Let me know which model families you want to target and I can attach model-specific token/accounting numbers and a small test script.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
